newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs down on selling by banks in volatile trading.
newsitem.headline: JGBs down on selling by banks in volatile trading.

text.p: The key December Japanese government bond (JGB) contract ended with substantial losses on corrective selling led by city banks, traders said on Monday.
The December ended at 123.55, down from Friday's 123.96. Turnover was a moderate 43,122 contracts.

"The market was volatile throughout the session, with little clue to a direction. Traders were reluctant to built fresh positions ahead of the machinery orders (data due on Tuesday)," said a European bank trader.
September machinery orders and the outlook for the October-December quarter are due at 0500 GMT on Tuesday.
Foreign speculators were generally on the buy side as they covered short positions built against their positions in interest rate swaps which they had unwound, traders said.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto was due to meet Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka from around 3.30 p.m. (0630 GMT) and call for drastic reform of Japan's financial system, a government official told Reuters. Justice Minister Isao Matsuura will also be asked to attend, the official said.
Traders said the market was unlikely to move unless the meeting offers immediate deregulatory steps with regard to taxes.
Banking industries have long called for an imminent scrapping of the securities transaction tax, which they describe as being one of major obstacles to the internationalisation of Tokyo's markets.
In the cash market, bargain hunting demand seen par for the 2.9 percent 190th JGB, limiting losses on cash bonds, traders said.
The yield of the key 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.760 percent, up from 2.710 percent at the close on Friday.
Market forecasts for the September machinery orders range widely from minus 7.8 percent to growth of 19.9 percent.
Most investors were content to stay on the sidelines ahead of the machinery orders and in the face of high volatility in the JGB market.
In the interest rate swap market, the five-year swap rate was quoted at 2.15/2.19 percent, up from 2.11/2.15 percent on Friday and compared with 1.84/1.88 percent a week ago.
